signals.distinguish_by: Re-add the displayed products; if they are right, the gap is arithmetic rather than conceptual.
signals.name: Correct Riemann sum products with an arithmetic slip in the total
signals.observation: All six factors of the sum are correct but the reported total does not match the products.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the widths alone; a correct width list points to a copying slip rather than a prerequisite gap.
signals.name: Single width applied across unequal subintervals
signals.observation: Every tabulated value is multiplied by the same number although the table inputs are unevenly spaced.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for both conventions; producing both correctly indicates a misread rather than a missing distinction.
signals.name: Correct sum of the opposite endpoint type
signals.observation: A fully correct Riemann sum is produced using the endpoint convention that was not requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of one term; rate units confirm the missing width factor.
signals.name: Sum of table values with no widths
signals.observation: The response adds the rate values and reports the total with the units of the rate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for a single trapezoid area; a correct one indicates a dropped factor rather than a missing formula.
signals.name: Left and right sums averaged without the halving
signals.observation: The trapezoidal answer equals the sum of the left and right sums.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which property of the rate supports the claim; a correct property indicates omission under time pressure.
signals.name: Direction of an estimate asserted with no stated reason
signals.observation: The words underestimate or overestimate appear with no reference to increase, decrease, or bending.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the direction on an increasing concave down rate; a correct answer there separates a slip from the conflation.
signals.name: Monotonicity cited for a trapezoidal estimate
signals.observation: The justification for a trapezoidal direction names increase or decrease rather than concavity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve the figure shows; a correct naming with the same answers points to the rule confusion instead.
signals.name: Features of the accumulation function read off the plotted curve
signals.observation: Reported extrema of g coincide with the visible extrema of the plotted integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the extrema of g in the same breath; identical lists confirm the single rule applied twice.
signals.name: Inflection points of the accumulation function placed at zeros of the integrand
signals.observation: The reported inflection inputs are exactly the inputs where the plotted curve crosses the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what feature of the figure makes the claim true; a correct answer confirms a communication gap.
signals.name: Correct feature list with a reason phrased only in terms of the accumulation function
signals.observation: The inputs are right and the stated reason names g changing concavity rather than the behaviour of the plotted integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether an endpoint could give a smaller value and how that is ruled out.
signals.name: Correct absolute extremum value with a local justification
signals.observation: The reported input is correct and the argument is a first or second derivative test at that input alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the complete candidate list before any evaluation; a complete list indicates an omission rather than a missing rule.
signals.name: Candidates table missing an endpoint
signals.observation: The comparison lists the interior critical inputs but omits one or both endpoints.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the integral before any arithmetic; a correct sign points to an arithmetic slip.
signals.name: Signed integral reported as a plain area
signals.observation: The reported value equals the sum of the unsigned areas although part of the region lies below the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of that single piece; a correct area indicates a dropped factor.
signals.name: Semicircular contribution doubled
signals.observation: The reported value differs from the correct one by exactly the area of half a circle.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the integral alone measures; a correct answer indicates the initial value was forgotten rather than misunderstood.
signals.name: Accumulated change reported as the final value
signals.observation: The reported value equals the definite integral of the rate and the supplied initial value does not appear anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the answer; rate times input units confirm the missing division.
signals.name: Integral reported where an average value was requested
signals.observation: The reported value equals the definite integral and no division by the interval length appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Present both phrases and ask which expression matches which.
signals.name: Difference quotient reported where an average value was requested
signals.observation: The reported value is a difference of function values divided by the interval length, with no integral present.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two converted limits; producing them correctly points to an omitted step.
signals.name: Original limits substituted into an expression written in the substituted variable
signals.observation: The work shows the antiderivative in u with the original x limits attached.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to differentiate the answer and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Answer differs from the correct antiderivative by a constant factor
signals.observation: The reported antiderivative is a nonzero constant multiple of the correct one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to differentiate the answer; recognising the mismatch indicates a procedural rather than conceptual gap.
signals.name: Product antidifferentiated factor by factor
signals.observation: The reported antiderivative is the product of the antiderivatives of the two factors.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to rewrite the integral as a limit; a correct rewrite indicates a notation habit.
signals.name: Improper integral evaluated by substituting infinity
signals.observation: The work shows the antiderivative evaluated at infinity with no limit notation anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the upper limit alone; a correct value points to an omission.
signals.name: Chain rule factor missing from the derivative of an accumulation function
signals.observation: The reported derivative is the integrand evaluated at the composite upper limit with no extra factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Vary the representation of the rate to confirm the skill transfers across a table, a graph, and a formula.
signals.name: Complete and correct multi step accumulation response
signals.observation: The integral, the initial condition, and the final value are all present with correct units.

signals.distinguish_by: Move the fixed lower limit away from an endpoint to confirm the reasoning is not anchored to one configuration.
signals.name: Complete accumulation function analysis with graph tied reasons
signals.observation: Every part names the feature of the plotted integrand that supports the claim about the accumulation function.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the inner function alone; a correct answer points to an omission rather than to an absent concept.
signals.name: Outer derivative correct with no inner factor
signals.observation: The response shows the derivative of the outer function evaluated at the inner expression and nothing else.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to list the layers in order; a correct list points to a bookkeeping slip.
signals.name: All layers present with one factor misplaced
signals.observation: Every layer has been differentiated but one factor is evaluated at the wrong expression or attached to the wrong term.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the inner function on its own before the derivative is requested.
signals.name: Chain rule written symbolically then evaluated at one input
signals.observation: The symbolic chain rule is correct but both derivatives are read at the same input from the table or the graph.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to differentiate the mixed term alone and to name the rule used.
signals.name: Some y terms carry dy/dx and others do not
signals.observation: The implicit differentiation attaches the factor to isolated y terms but not to the y inside a mixed product.

signals.distinguish_by: Present a differentiated equation already written and ask only for the algebra; success points to a procedural gap rather than a calculus one.
signals.name: Differentiated equation correct but never solved for dy/dx
signals.observation: The response stops at a correct differentiated equation without collecting or factoring the dy/dx terms.

signals.distinguish_by: Re-substitute the coordinates; if the arithmetic then works out, the gap is arithmetic rather than conceptual.
signals.name: Correct dy/dx with a substitution slip at the point
signals.observation: The expression for dy/dx is correct but the reported slope does not follow from substituting the stated coordinates.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the reported value determines a point, and how many points it determines.
signals.name: Tangent condition solved but the curve equation not used
signals.observation: The correct condition on dy/dx is set and solved, and the response stops without substituting into the defining equation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the formula when the original derivative is zero at the matching input.
signals.name: Inverse rule written without the nonzero condition
signals.observation: The reciprocal formula is stated correctly and no condition on the original derivative is mentioned.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the matching input alone; a correct answer points to a slip rather than to a gap in the inverse function idea.
signals.name: Reciprocal taken at the wrong input
signals.observation: The response reports the reciprocal of the derivative of the original function at the value supplied in the prompt.

signals.distinguish_by: Replace the inner expression by a single letter and ask for the derivative again.
signals.name: Correct inverse trigonometric formula with the inner expression missing
signals.observation: The standard formula appears with the variable in place of the inner expression, or without the inner derivative factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name the operation applied last when the expression is evaluated at a number.
signals.name: Correct rules applied in the wrong order
signals.observation: Every rule the expression needs appears in the work but the nesting order is wrong, so the factors attach to the wrong pieces.

signals.distinguish_by: Compare the two lines at a single numerical input to locate the algebra slip.
signals.name: Correct derivative spoiled by a later simplification
signals.observation: A correct derivative appears on one line and an incorrect simplified form on the next.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to restate the order requested before checking the work.
signals.name: Differentiation stops one order short
signals.observation: The work is correct as far as it goes but the reported derivative is one order lower than the order requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to read the line aloud and to name each symbol.
signals.name: Notation mixed within a single line
signals.observation: Prime notation and Leibniz notation appear in the same equation in ways that do not agree.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the first derivative at the point as a separate question.
signals.name: Product and chain rules correct with the first derivative value omitted
signals.observation: The second derivative expression is fully correct and the numerical evaluation ignores the value of the first derivative at the point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the comparison step alone; a correct comparison indicates a communication slip rather than a gap.
signals.name: One sided values correct with a two sided claim attached
signals.observation: Both one sided limits are reported correctly but the response then names one of them as the two sided limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two quantities separately and in the opposite order.
signals.name: Limit and value swapped at a marked break
signals.observation: The response reports the plotted value as the limit and the limit as the value.

signals.distinguish_by: Re-evaluate the simplified expression; if it is right, the gap is arithmetic rather than conceptual.
signals.name: Correct rewriting with an arithmetic slip in the final evaluation
signals.observation: The factorisation and cancellation are correct but the value obtained by substituting into the simplified expression is wrong.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the factorisation of numerator and denominator; success indicates the gap is in knowing what the form signals.
signals.name: Indeterminate form named and then abandoned
signals.observation: The response identifies the form as zero over zero and reports that the limit does not exist without attempting a rewriting.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the limits of numerator and denominator separately; success indicates a notation habit rather than a gap (sg-23:14).
signals.name: Limit written as equal to zero over zero with correct subsequent work
signals.observation: The response writes the limit equal to the indeterminate symbol but then rewrites correctly and reaches the right value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the listed conditions has been verified and which has not.
signals.name: Three conditions listed but only one checked
signals.observation: The response states the definition of continuity in full and then tests only the function value or only the limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the function value at the boundary and then for the conclusion again.
signals.name: Correct branch limits with the wrong conclusion about continuity
signals.observation: Both one sided limits at the boundary are correct but the conclusion ignores the defined value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which branch supplies the function value at the boundary.
signals.name: Parameter solved from the limits with the function value unchecked
signals.observation: A value of the constant is produced that matches the one sided limits but the branch that defines the value at the boundary is not considered.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the factorisation first; success afterwards indicates a missing step rather than a missing idea.
signals.name: Asymptote located without simplification
signals.observation: Every zero of the original denominator is reported as an asymptote although one factor divides out.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the quotient on each side separately.
signals.name: Correct asymptote with a single two sided infinite statement
signals.observation: The location of the vertical asymptote is right but the behaviour is written as one two sided infinite limit where the sides differ.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the expression alone; the separate point for the expression is not covered by a correct value (sg-25:4).
signals.name: End behaviour value correct with no limit expression presented
signals.observation: The response reports the correct end behaviour value but never writes the limit expression that the question asks for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the quantity inside the limit; a response presenting the limit of the amount is not eligible for the value point (sg-25:4).
signals.name: Limit expression written for the amount rather than the rate
signals.observation: The limit expression names the modelled quantity although the question asks about its rate of change.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what property of the function given in the question makes it continuous; the continuity point requires that reason while the conclusion point does not depend on it (sg-25:12).
signals.name: Straddling inequality correct with continuity asserted bare
signals.observation: The two attained values on either side of the target are displayed correctly but the continuity statement carries no reason.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two function values that the target lies between.
signals.name: Continuity justified correctly with no straddling values shown
signals.observation: The response says the function is continuous because it is differentiable but never displays the two values that bracket the target.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether a second input could give the same value and what would rule it out.
signals.name: Existence argument complete but phrased as a unique solution
signals.observation: All hypotheses are verified and the conclusion is stated, but the response claims exactly one input gives the target value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the computed values as the interval keeps shrinking.
signals.name: Average rates computed correctly with no limiting statement
signals.observation: The sequence of average rates is correct but the response never says what those values approach.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the function has a value at that endpoint.
signals.name: Intervals of continuity correct with a closed bracket at an excluded input
signals.observation: The pieces of the domain are identified correctly but one endpoint is written as included.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the limits of the two bounding functions as separate answers.
signals.name: Squeeze bounds correct with the conclusion drawn from evaluation
signals.observation: The bounding inequality is established correctly but the conclusion substitutes the target into the bounds rather than taking their limits.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the harmonic series does; a student who then withdraws the claim was reading quickly rather than holding the converse.
signals.name: The response states that the terms approach zero and concludes that the series converges,
signals.observation: The response states that the terms approach zero and concludes that the series converges, with no other test applied.

signals.distinguish_by: The ratio point is banked while the limit point is not, so the gap is in the limit rather than in the setup (sg-25:25).
signals.name: The ratio of consecutive terms is correct but the limit is evaluated incorrectly
signals.observation: The ratio of consecutive terms is correct but the limit is evaluated incorrectly.

signals.distinguish_by: A reciprocal ratio earns the setup point and keeps the interior and endpoint points in reach but not the final interval point (sg-25:25).
signals.name: The reciprocal of the required ratio is presented and carried through consistently
signals.observation: The reciprocal of the required ratio is presented and carried through consistently.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the series becomes at one endpoint; fluent substitution points to time pressure rather than to the belief that the interior is the interval.
signals.name: The open interval is reported as the interval of convergence with no endpoint work shown
signals.observation: The open interval is reported as the interval of convergence with no endpoint work shown.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write both endpoint series side by side and compare their forms.
signals.name: One endpoint is tested correctly and the verdict is transferred to the other without a sec
signals.observation: One endpoint is tested correctly and the verdict is transferred to the other without a second test.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which condition of the named test the endpoint series fails.
signals.name: An endpoint series of positive terms is analysed with the alternating series test, or an a
signals.observation: An endpoint series of positive terms is analysed with the alternating series test, or an alternating one with a direct comparison.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two inequalities the absolute value statement stands for (sg-22:21).
signals.name: The inequality is solved without absolute value and a one sided interval is reported
signals.observation: The inequality is solved without absolute value and a one sided interval is reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how far the interval reaches from its centre; an immediate answer shows the gap is in reading the request (sg-21:24).
signals.name: A correct interval is presented where the radius was requested, with no value named as the
signals.observation: A correct interval is presented where the radius was requested, with no value named as the radius.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which three properties the test requires; the conditions point needs all three (sg-21:22).
signals.name: Two of the three integral test conditions are listed and the third is omitted
signals.observation: Two of the three integral test conditions are listed and the third is omitted.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to rewrite the evaluation with an upper bound b before the limit (sg-21:22).
signals.name: The antiderivative is evaluated by substituting the infinity symbol rather than by taking
signals.observation: The antiderivative is evaluated by substituting the infinity symbol rather than by taking a limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the test concludes when the limit is three; the setup is sound and the criterion is the gap (sg-21:23).
signals.name: The limit comparison ratio is evaluated correctly and then compared with one to reach the
signals.observation: The limit comparison ratio is evaluated correctly and then compared with one to reach the conclusion.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to point at the series the sentence is about (sg-21:23).
signals.name: The conclusion states that the series converges absolutely without identifying which of th
signals.observation: The conclusion states that the series converges absolutely without identifying which of the several series in the part is meant.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which series has the larger terms and what each direction implies (sg-24:20).
signals.name: A correct comparison series is chosen but the inequality is stated in the direction that d
signals.observation: A correct comparison series is chosen but the inequality is stated in the direction that does not support the conclusion.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the error is known exactly; the bounding term is right and the relation is the gap (sg-22:21).
signals.name: The correct bounding term is found and the error is then written as equal to it
signals.observation: The correct bounding term is found and the error is then written as equal to it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what has to be true before the bound may be used (sg-24:21).
signals.name: The bound is applied with the correct term and the alternating and decreasing conditions a
signals.observation: The bound is applied with the correct term and the alternating and decreasing conditions are never stated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which terms the partial sum already contains (sg-22:21).
signals.name: A term of higher degree than the first omitted one is used as the bound
signals.observation: A term of higher degree than the first omitted one is used as the bound.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which derivative the bound for a fourth degree polynomial uses (sg-23:20).
signals.name: The bound is assembled with the derivative of the same order as the polynomial rather than
signals.observation: The bound is assembled with the derivative of the same order as the polynomial rather than one order higher.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the coefficient produced by a second derivative of six (sg-23:19).
signals.name: Derivative values appear directly as coefficients with no factorial denominators
signals.observation: Derivative values appear directly as coefficients with no factorial denominators.

signals.distinguish_by: The form point is earned and the derivative point is not, and the response may still use its own value consistently (sg-23:19).
signals.name: The form of the product rule is displayed correctly but the resulting derivative expressio
signals.observation: The form of the product rule is displayed correctly but the resulting derivative expression is incomplete.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what degree was requested; the coefficients are sound and the presentation is the gap (sg-23:20).
signals.name: The requested polynomial is correct through the requested degree and carries an extra term
signals.observation: The requested polynomial is correct through the requested degree and carries an extra term or a trailing ellipsis.

signals.distinguish_by: Substitute the first two index values into the proposed general term and compare (sg-25:26).
signals.name: The first nonzero terms are correct and the general term does not reproduce them
signals.observation: The first nonzero terms are correct and the general term does not reproduce them.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the CED guarantees about the radius of a term-by-term derivative (sg-24:22).
signals.name: The differentiated series is correct and its radius is recomputed to a value inconsistent
signals.observation: The differentiated series is correct and its radius is recomputed to a value inconsistent with the original.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the input sits relative to the interval; a fluent answer points to time pressure (sg-25:27).
signals.name: The verdict about convergence at a specific input is correct and no reason is attached
signals.observation: The verdict about convergence at a specific input is correct and no reason is attached.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the next partial sum and whether both totals can be the value of the series.
signals.name: The first several terms are added and the total is reported as the value of the series
signals.observation: The first several terms are added and the total is reported as the value of the series.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the same average over an interval of length one; a correct answer there with a wrong answer elsewhere points at the missing division rather than at the integral.
signals.name: Correct integral with no division by the interval length
signals.observation: The response shows the correct definite integral and reports its value, with no quotient anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the reported answer; rate units confirm the confusion with average rate of change.
signals.name: Difference quotient produced where an average value was requested
signals.observation: The response computes the change in the function divided by the change in the input and calls it the average value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the displacement in the same part; a correct displacement with an equal answer for distance isolates the integrand choice.
signals.name: Signed integral reported as total distance
signals.observation: The response integrates velocity across a sign change and reports the result as the distance travelled.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the same question with a different starting amount; an unchanged answer confirms that the initial value is not in the model.
signals.name: Accumulated change reported where an amount was asked
signals.observation: The definite integral is evaluated correctly and reported without the known value at the earlier time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the amount at each endpoint; producing them on request separates a reporting gap from a conceptual one.
signals.name: Critical point found with only a local justification
signals.observation: The derivative is set equal to zero and solved correctly, and the justification is a sign chart with no endpoint comparison and no uniqueness statement.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the sentence would be for a different pair of limits; a correct second sentence points at a communication habit rather than a concept gap.
signals.name: Interpretation naming the quantity and units but not the interval
signals.observation: The sentence gives the accumulated quantity with correct units and omits the two inputs bounding the accumulation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve is above the other at one interior input; a correct answer there isolates the sign slip.
signals.name: Negative value reported as an area or a volume
signals.observation: The integral is set up with the difference in the wrong order and the reported value is negative.

signals.distinguish_by: Recompute with the stored values; agreement confirms a rounding habit rather than a set up error.
signals.name: Stored intersection values replaced by rounded decimals
signals.observation: The limits appear as two or three place decimals and the reported area differs from the correct value in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name the variable of integration and to list the variables in the integrand.
signals.name: Differential dy attached to an integrand written in x
signals.observation: The integral carries dy with an integrand that still contains x, and the limits may be x values.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the integrand just above and just below the crossing.
signals.name: One integral spanning an interior crossing
signals.observation: The response writes one integral of a fixed difference over an interval in which the curves exchange places.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which shape the area formula inside the integral belongs to.
signals.name: Factor of pi in a polygonal cross section integrand
signals.observation: The volume integral for square or triangular sections carries pi.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a semicircle of stated radius; a correct answer isolates the radius error from the halving error.
signals.name: Full circle area used for a semicircular section
signals.observation: The integrand is pi times the square of half the distance with no factor of one half, or pi times the square of the whole distance.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of one circular slice before the integral is assembled.
signals.name: Solid of revolution volume reported without pi
signals.observation: The integrand is the square of the radius with no constant factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to compute both expressions with the radii five and three.
signals.name: Washer integrand written as one squared difference
signals.observation: The integrand is pi times the square of the difference of the two functions.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the distance from a named point on the curve to the axis of revolution.
signals.name: Radius written as the bare function value about a shifted axis
signals.observation: The axis of revolution is a line other than a coordinate axis and the radius in the integrand contains no reference to it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve is farther from the axis at one interior input.
signals.name: Negative volume from exchanged radii
signals.observation: The washer integral evaluates to a negative number and the response reports it or its absolute value without comment.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the limits of integration describe; naming them on request separates a reporting gap from a concept gap.
signals.name: Arc length named with no interval
signals.observation: The response says the integral gives the length of the curve and stops.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the conditions; a student who states them on request has a communication gap, not a conceptual one.
signals.name: Conclusion correct with no hypothesis sentence
signals.observation: The answer and the arithmetic are right but no sentence establishes continuity or differentiability.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the computed quantity.
signals.name: Endpoint values averaged instead of a difference quotient
signals.observation: The reported average rate of change is the mean of the two function values.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity the cited theorem makes a claim about.
signals.name: Existence argued with the wrong theorem named
signals.observation: The arithmetic supports the conclusion but the theorem cited concerns values of the function.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the reported input lies strictly inside the interval.
signals.name: Correct equation solved with a root outside the interval reported
signals.observation: The derivative equation is set up correctly but the reported input is an endpoint or lies outside.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the continuity claim comes from in the given information.
signals.name: Continuity asserted with no support
signals.observation: The response says the function is continuous and offers nothing that establishes it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the theorem asserts and what it leaves open.
signals.name: Existence question answered with a located extremum
signals.observation: The response names an input instead of asserting that extreme values are attained.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what equation produced the listed inputs.
signals.name: Zeros listed with no derivative equation presented
signals.observation: Correct critical inputs appear with no equation showing the derivative set equal to zero.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to mark every input where the derivative graph breaks.
signals.name: Critical point list missing the non-differentiable input
signals.observation: Every zero of the derivative is present and the corner or cusp is absent.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether an endpoint could beat the reported value.
signals.name: Local claim offered for a global question
signals.observation: The response identifies a relative extremum correctly and presents it as the answer to an absolute extremum question.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the derivative immediately on each side.
signals.name: Extremum declared where the derivative touches zero
signals.observation: The response reports a relative extremum at an input where the derivative keeps its sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for a test value inside the disputed interval.
signals.name: Sign chart correct except on one interval
signals.observation: All partition points are right and one interval carries the wrong sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function the drawn curve represents.
signals.name: Answer describes the plotted curve rather than the function
signals.observation: The intervals reported are those on which the drawn curve rises, when the drawn curve is the derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which expression must change sign for the behaviour in question.
signals.name: Partition points taken from the function rather than the derivative
signals.observation: The number line is split at the zeros of the function.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to replace every pronoun with a name.
signals.name: Correct intervals with an unnamed referent in the reason
signals.observation: The intervals are right and the sentence says the function or the graph without saying which.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the function has a value at the input between them.
signals.name: Interval reported across an input where the function is undefined
signals.observation: Two correct stretches are merged into one interval spanning a domain gap.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to sketch the curve implied by their own sentence.
signals.name: Classification reversed with a correct sign statement
signals.observation: The sign change is described correctly and the conclusion is the opposite kind of extremum.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for both the input and the value.
signals.name: Correct extremum with the wrong quantity reported
signals.observation: The work locates the extremum correctly and the reported answer is the input where the value was asked for, or the reverse.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the function value at each end of the interval.
signals.name: Candidate list missing an endpoint
signals.observation: The critical points are all present and one or both endpoints are absent from the comparison.

signals.distinguish_by: Recompute the disputed entry; if the rest are right the gap is arithmetic.
signals.name: Candidate table with one wrong entry
signals.observation: The candidate list is complete and one evaluation does not match the given information.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which tabulated value is smallest.
signals.name: Comparison made in the wrong direction
signals.observation: A correct candidate table is followed by the wrong selection.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how the candidate compares with the far endpoint.
signals.name: Justification built from a local test
signals.observation: The answer is right and the justification is a first or second derivative test at the candidate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for a test value of the second derivative inside the disputed interval.
signals.name: Concavity intervals correct with the wrong sign reported once
signals.observation: The partition is right and one interval is labelled with the wrong concavity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the plotted curve is rising or falling on that stretch.
signals.name: Concavity reported where the derivative is positive
signals.observation: The intervals reported are the intervals on which the plotted derivative lies above the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the function has a value there.
signals.name: Candidate inflection list includes an input outside the domain
signals.observation: An input where the function is undefined appears in the list.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the second derivative does on each side of each listed input.
signals.name: Every zero of the second derivative declared an inflection point
signals.observation: The list matches the zeros exactly with no sign change discussed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the second derivative on both sides of the extra input.
signals.name: One extra input in an otherwise correct inflection list
signals.observation: Two of three listed inputs are correct and a touching zero has been retained.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which plotted feature makes that sign change happen.
signals.name: Correct list with the reason phrased in second derivative symbols
signals.observation: The inputs are exactly right and the reason cites a sign change of the second derivative rather than the given plotted function.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which way the curve bends when the second derivative is negative.
signals.name: Second derivative evaluated correctly with the classification reversed
signals.observation: The numerical second derivative is right and the reported extremum type is the opposite one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the first derivative does on each side.
signals.name: Zero second derivative read as a verdict
signals.observation: The response concludes neither because the second derivative vanishes at the critical point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many critical points lie in the interval.
signals.name: Global claim made with no uniqueness statement
signals.observation: The relative extremum is extended to an absolute one without saying that it is the only critical point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which derivative the given object shows.
signals.name: Test chosen that the given object cannot supply
signals.observation: A second derivative test is begun from a graph of the first derivative with no discussion of its slope.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the original curve has a horizontal tangent.
signals.name: Derivative sketch with extrema at the zeros of the function
signals.observation: The drawn derivative turns where the original curve crosses the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the derivative equals at a relative maximum of the function.
signals.name: Sketch with extrema and inflection points interchanged
signals.observation: The drawn function turns where the given derivative turns instead of where it crosses the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which derivative must change sign for an extremum and which for a point of inflection.
signals.name: Feature matched one derivative away
signals.observation: Every correspondence the response gives is displaced by one derivative in the same direction.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether shifting the sketch vertically would still fit the derivative.
signals.name: Sketch presented as the only possible curve
signals.observation: The response asserts a unique graph of the function from derivative information alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve has zeros at the turning points of which.
signals.name: Three graphs labelled in the reverse order
signals.observation: The assignment is internally consistent and runs in the opposite derivative direction.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign, not the direction, of the second derivative.
signals.name: Second derivative statement translated into the wrong shape claim
signals.observation: A correct statement about the second derivative is turned into the opposite concavity claim.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the second derivative at one input in the disputed piece.
signals.name: Combined sign table with one row correct
signals.observation: The first derivative row is right throughout and the second derivative row is wrong on at least one piece.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether another function through the same table could behave differently.
signals.name: Behaviour claimed between tabulated inputs
signals.observation: The response asserts monotonicity or concavity across a whole interval from three tabulated values.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units.
signals.name: Objective written with undefined letters
signals.observation: An expression to be optimised appears in symbols that are never given meanings.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many unknowns remain before differentiating.
signals.name: Two variables carried into the differentiation
signals.observation: The expression differentiated still contains both unknowns.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which values of the variable make sense in the situation.
signals.name: No contextual domain stated
signals.observation: The reduced objective is optimised with no statement of which inputs the situation allows.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how the student knows it is a maximum rather than a minimum.
signals.name: Critical point reported with no verification
signals.observation: The derivative is set to zero, solved, and the value is announced as the extremum.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the number measures.
signals.name: Optimal value reported without units
signals.observation: A correct number appears with no unit attached in an applied context.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different.
signals.name: Interpretation naming the quantity only
signals.observation: The sentence names the modelled quantity and omits the units or the input at which the extremum occurs.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the denominator at the reported point.
signals.name: Numerator zeros reported with no denominator check
signals.observation: Points where both the numerator and the denominator of the derivative vanish appear as horizontal tangents.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the reported coordinates satisfy the relation.
signals.name: Denominator zeros reported without checking the relation
signals.observation: Solutions of the denominator equation are listed without testing them in the defining equation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which outputs the relation pairs with that input.
signals.name: One coordinate reported for a point on a relation
signals.observation: An input value is given as the answer where a point on the curve was asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the square of the dependent variable.
signals.name: Second derivative taken with the dependent variable held fixed
signals.observation: The differentiation omits the chain rule factor on the dependent variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the first derivative at the point, then reread the expression.
signals.name: Derivative symbol left in a numerical answer
signals.observation: The reported second derivative value still contains the first derivative symbol.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the reported number; a correct unit statement afterwards indicates a communication slip rather than a gap (sg-25:11).
signals.name: Correct difference with the division omitted
signals.observation: The two tabulated values are subtracted correctly but the result is reported without dividing by the change in the inputs.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the written expression; the expression alone does not earn the answer point (sg-25:11).
signals.name: Correct quotient with no value reported
signals.observation: The difference quotient is set up correctly from the right rows but is never evaluated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the denominator of the quotient measures.
signals.name: Correct estimate with the units of the quantity attached
signals.observation: The numerical estimate is correct but the units given are those of the modelled quantity rather than of its rate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the algebraic simplification of the numerator before any substitution.
signals.name: Difference quotient set up correctly then collapsed
signals.observation: The difference quotient is written correctly but the increment is set to zero while it is still in the denominator.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to read one intermediate line aloud as a claim; a correct correction indicates a notation habit rather than a gap.
signals.name: Correct derivative with the limit symbol absent from the work
signals.observation: The value obtained is correct but the intermediate lines carry no limit symbol.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which value of the function is subtracted in the numerator.
signals.name: Limit identified as a derivative with the wrong base point
signals.observation: The underlying function is named correctly but the derivative is evaluated at the wrong input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what property stated in the question makes the function continuous; the continuity point requires that reason (sg-25:12).
signals.name: Continuity used correctly but stated without its reason
signals.observation: The argument proceeds correctly from continuity but the response never says that continuity follows from differentiability.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for a function continuous at a point at which it has no derivative.
signals.name: Implication stated in the wrong direction
signals.observation: The response asserts that the function is differentiable because it is continuous.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the one sided slopes as two numbers.
signals.name: Correct verdict on differentiability with a visual reason
signals.observation: The response correctly says the derivative does not exist but supports it only by the appearance of the graph.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of a single squared term from the definition.
signals.name: Exponents reduced correctly with the coefficients dropped
signals.observation: Every exponent is lowered by one but no term is multiplied by its original exponent.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to rewrite the untouched term as a power of the variable first.
signals.name: Polynomial terms differentiated with a radical term copied
signals.observation: The polynomial part of the expression is differentiated correctly while a radical or reciprocal term is carried through unchanged.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the slope of the graph just to the right of the origin.
signals.name: Trigonometric derivative correct except for the sign
signals.observation: The derivative of a sine or cosine term is right in form but carries the wrong sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to label each supplied number before substituting.
signals.name: Product rule written correctly with one derivative value misread
signals.observation: The rule is set out with the names in the right positions but one of the four supplied numbers is a function value where a derivative value belongs.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to apply the rule to a reciprocal and compare with the power rule result.
signals.name: Quotient rule applied with the numerator terms reversed
signals.observation: The structure of the quotient rule is right but the subtraction runs the wrong way, so the answer differs only in sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rule applies to the rewritten expression.
signals.name: Trigonometric rewriting correct with the quotient rule misapplied
signals.observation: The function is rewritten correctly with sine and cosine but the differentiation that follows is done term by term.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which input the line touches the curve and what the height is there.
signals.name: Tangent line correct in slope but through the wrong point
signals.observation: The derivative is evaluated correctly but the point used in the line equation is not the point of tangency.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the expression the calculator evaluated; the setup carries its own point (sg-25:4).
signals.name: Calculator value correct with no setup shown
signals.observation: A correct numerical derivative is reported with nothing indicating what was computed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units alone; a correct answer points to an omission under time pressure rather than a gap.
signals.name: Correct rate reported with no units
signals.observation: The numerical rate is right and no units accompany it anywhere in the part.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two the units in the stem describe; a correct answer points to a misread.
signals.name: Function value supplied where a rate was requested
signals.observation: The answer is a value of the model and the question asked for its rate of change.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two table entries were used; a correct answer points to omitted communication rather than to a gap.
signals.name: Bare quotient with no difference shown
signals.observation: A single number or a quotient appears with no visible subtraction of tabulated values.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function the stem supplied and which one the question wants.
signals.name: Correct differentiation of the wrong order
signals.observation: The differentiation performed is correct and produces a quantity other than the one requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether a speed can be negative and what the sign records instead.
signals.name: Negative number reported as a speed
signals.observation: The response gives a speed with a minus sign attached.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity must be negative for motion in the negative direction.
signals.name: Direction argued from the wrong function
signals.observation: The conclusion about direction of travel rests on the sign of the position rather than of the velocity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the velocity at that instant and whether it changes the conclusion.
signals.name: Only the acceleration sign cited for a speed conclusion
signals.observation: The speed conclusion names the sign of the acceleration and does not name the sign of the velocity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to state the conclusion in one sentence; a correct sentence points to a communication gap.
signals.name: Sign chart with no stated conclusion
signals.observation: A correct sign chart appears and no sentence states what it shows about the interval in the prompt.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the letters in the model stand for.
signals.name: Computation correct with the context never named
signals.observation: The mathematics is right and no sentence identifies the quantity, its units, or its independent variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the limit expression that supports the value.
signals.name: Correct value with infinity written in place of a limit
signals.observation: The value of the end behaviour is right and the supporting line substitutes infinity into the expression.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write each supplied rate in derivative notation; success points to a translation gap rather than a calculus one.
signals.name: Rates not written in derivative notation
signals.observation: The scenario is restated in words and no quantity appears as a derivative with respect to time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the formula for the named quantity with no calculus involved.
signals.name: Relating equation absent or mismatched to the figure
signals.observation: The response differentiates something that does not describe the configuration, or differentiates nothing.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must be multiplied by that derivative to reach the rate with respect to time.
signals.name: Differentiation stops at the derivative with respect to a length
signals.observation: The relation is differentiated with respect to a spatial variable and no chain rule step reaches the rate with respect to time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the stated numbers would still hold one second later.
signals.name: Instantaneous values present before the differentiation
signals.observation: A varying dimension appears as a number in the equation that is then differentiated.

signals.distinguish_by: Present the substituted equation and ask only for the algebra.
signals.name: Correct differentiated equation with the rate never isolated
signals.observation: The substitution is complete and the response stops before solving for the requested rate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line they wrote.
signals.name: Correct slope with a tangent line assembly error
signals.observation: The slope at the point of tangency is right and the line written does not pass through the point.

signals.distinguish_by: Change the example to an increasing concave down function and ask again; a changed answer points to a guess.
signals.name: Correct direction of error with an increase or decrease reason
signals.observation: The over or under estimate claim is right and the reason given is that the function is increasing or decreasing.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what has to be true for the rule to apply and whether the response showed it.
signals.name: Rule applied with the form never verified
signals.observation: Derivatives of numerator and denominator appear and no separate limits establish the indeterminate form.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the numerator alone; the 2023 report records this as the point at which otherwise correct responses failed (cr-23:15).
signals.name: Hypothesis verified with an incorrect derivative
signals.observation: The two separate limits are correct and one of the two derivatives in the new quotient is wrong.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two component derivatives separately; producing them and the quotient on request points at a communication habit rather than a concept gap.
signals.name: Correct slope value with no quotient shown
signals.observation: A correct decimal for the slope appears with no expression showing dy/dt divided by dx/dt.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function was differentiated at the second step.
signals.name: Second derivative assembled from two second derivatives
signals.observation: The reported second derivative is the quotient of the second derivative of y by the second derivative of x with respect to the parameter.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the speed with component rates three and four; an answer of seven confirms the additive model.
signals.name: Component rates added inside a speed or length
signals.observation: The speed or arc length integrand is the sum of the two component rates.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for both quantities on a path that returns to its start; equal answers confirm the confusion.
signals.name: Magnitude of displacement reported as distance travelled
signals.observation: The response integrates the components first and takes a magnitude of the result.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative expressions; producing them on request separates a presentation habit from a gap.
signals.name: Correct vector with no supporting work
signals.observation: Two correct components appear with no differentiation and no evaluation shown.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the same question with a different known position; an unchanged answer confirms the missing initial value.
signals.name: Definite integral reported as a coordinate
signals.observation: The value of the integral of a velocity component is given as the coordinate, with the known position unused.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two times the position is known at and in which direction time runs between them.
signals.name: Accumulation added when the known time is later
signals.observation: The integral between the two times is added to the known coordinate although the known time is the later one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the equation that was solved; writing it correctly points at a presentation habit.
signals.name: Time reported with no equation
signals.observation: A correct time at which the speed takes the stated value appears alone on the page.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask why the particle approaches on that interval; a correct sign argument on request separates communication from concept.
signals.name: Correct interval of approach with no sign argument
signals.observation: The subinterval on which the particle approaches the axis is correct and no statement about the sign of the rate appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the derivative of r before evaluating it.
signals.name: Polar derivative value with no differentiation shown
signals.observation: A correct value for dr/dtheta appears with nothing indicating that r was differentiated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the coordinate at each endpoint of the angle interval.
signals.name: Critical angle found with only a local justification
signals.observation: The derivative of the coordinate is set equal to zero and solved correctly, and the justification is a derivative test with no endpoint comparison and no uniqueness statement.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a circular sector of stated radius and angle.
signals.name: Polar area integral without the factor of one half
signals.observation: The integrand is the square of r with no factor of one half, and the reported value is twice the area.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which angles the two curves meet.
signals.name: Polar area limits spanning the whole figure
signals.observation: The limits of the area integral are the ends of the interval in which the figure is drawn rather than the intersection angles.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what changes in the model if the quantity grows twice as fast.
signals.name: Model written with no constant of proportionality
signals.observation: The equation sets the rate equal to the quantity or the difference with no constant.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units.
signals.name: Equation written in undefined letters
signals.observation: The letters of the model are never given meanings or units.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which statement would change if the starting value were different.
signals.name: Initial condition absorbed into the equation
signals.observation: The stated value appears as a term of the differential equation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the left side of the written equation measures.
signals.name: Formula produced where an equation was asked for
signals.observation: The response gives an expression for the quantity rather than a relation involving its derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the left side of the differential equation requires.
signals.name: Candidate substituted without its derivative
signals.observation: The verification puts the candidate into both sides and no derivative appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the candidate gives at the stated input.
signals.name: Equation verified and the initial condition ignored
signals.observation: The substitution checks out and the stated point is never tested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for one input at which the two sides differ.
signals.name: Negative verdict with nothing exhibited
signals.observation: The response says the candidate fails and shows no disagreeing input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name two different functions satisfying the same equation.
signals.name: Family treated as a single function
signals.observation: The general solution with its constant is described as the solution.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the coordinates the slope was computed at.
signals.name: Slope computed at a neighbouring lattice point
signals.observation: The arithmetic is right for coordinates one grid step away from the one asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the numerical slope at two separated points.
signals.name: Field drawn with uniform segments
signals.observation: Every drawn segment has the same tilt regardless of position.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which values of the quantity make the rate zero.
signals.name: Zero slope locus never identified
signals.observation: The response works through the field or the equation without solving the right side equal to zero.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which variables appear in the right side.
signals.name: Dependence pattern misread from the field
signals.observation: The response claims the slope varies along a line on which the printed segments are identical.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the curve is tangent to the segment at each point it passes.
signals.name: Curve through the right point conflicting with the segments
signals.observation: The drawn curve starts correctly and its slope disagrees with nearby segments, or it stops short of an edge.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the rate of change is exactly at that level.
signals.name: Curve drawn across the equilibrium level
signals.observation: The sketch otherwise follows the field and rises through the row of horizontal segments.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the slope at a point where the candidates disagree.
signals.name: Equation matched on the look of the field
signals.observation: A candidate is chosen with no computed slope and no zero slope locus mentioned.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which feature of the field or the equation makes the claim true.
signals.name: Long-run claim with no supporting feature named
signals.observation: The response states where solutions are heading and cites neither the segments nor the sign of the rate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the differential equation says the first derivative equals.
signals.name: Second derivative left in terms of the first
signals.observation: The differentiated right side still contains the derivative symbol instead of the dependent variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how long each of the stated number of equal steps is.
signals.name: Whole interval used as one step
signals.observation: The arithmetic is right for a single step across the entire interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which point the slope is evaluated at on the first step.
signals.name: First step taken from the wrong point
signals.observation: The step size is right and the derivative is evaluated somewhere other than the initial condition.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the input and the output used at the start of the second step.
signals.name: Second step evaluated at the initial point
signals.observation: The first step is correct and the second uses the initial output again.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to label the columns of their own table.
signals.name: Bare value with no steps or labels
signals.observation: A single number, or an unlabelled table, is offered with no visible increments.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the second derivative does over the interval.
signals.name: Direction claimed with no concavity statement
signals.observation: The response names an overestimate or an underestimate and cites monotonicity or nothing at all.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which terms belong on which side before any integral is written.
signals.name: Integral signs written with both variables on one side
signals.observation: The antidifferentiation begins without the variables having been separated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happened to the differential on the other side.
signals.name: One side antidifferentiated correctly and the other untouched
signals.observation: The separated form is right and only one antiderivative appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the answer would be if the starting value were different.
signals.name: Antiderivative equation with no constant
signals.observation: Both antiderivatives are right and no constant of integration appears anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the dependent variable at a stated input.
signals.name: Correct antiderivative equation left unsolved
signals.observation: The constant is found and the dependent variable is never isolated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the right side as a product of two single variable factors.
signals.name: Separation attempted on a non-separable equation
signals.observation: Terms are moved across as though the right side factored when it is a sum in both variables.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which equation the initial values were substituted into.
signals.name: Initial condition substituted after exponentiating
signals.observation: The constant is evaluated in an expression where it has already changed form.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the enclosed expression is positive or negative at the initial point.
signals.name: Branch chosen against the initial condition
signals.observation: The absolute value is removed with the sign that contradicts the given point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens at the input where the expression fails to be defined.
signals.name: Solution reported with no interval
signals.observation: An explicit expression is given and no domain statement accompanies it although one was asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the expression gives at the initial input.
signals.name: Accumulation form written without the initial value
signals.observation: The particular solution is offered as an integral alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the answer should still contain a constant.
signals.name: Answer of the wrong kind for the question
signals.observation: A constant remains where a particular solution was asked for, or is fixed where the general solution was.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the rate when the amount doubles.
signals.name: Linear model offered for proportional growth
signals.observation: The quantity is written as the initial value plus a constant multiple of the independent variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the formula gives at the initial input.
signals.name: Exponential written with the constants misplaced
signals.observation: The initial value appears inside the exponent, or the rate constant outside it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two pieces of data the constant needs.
signals.name: Rate constant produced from the initial condition alone
signals.observation: A numerical constant is reported with only one data pair used.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the number measures and whether the quantity is rising.
signals.name: Constant reported with no direction or units
signals.observation: The number is given and the response does not say whether the quantity grows or decays.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity the differential equation constrains.
signals.name: Motion quantity reported one derivative away
signals.observation: A velocity is reported where a position was asked for, or the reverse.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the rate when the quantity reaches the capacity.
signals.name: Logistic equation written without the limiting factor
signals.observation: The model is a constant multiple of the quantity alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which nonzero value of the quantity makes the rate zero.
signals.name: Wrong factor read as the carrying capacity
signals.observation: The constant of proportionality, or zero, is reported as the capacity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which values of the quantity make the rate positive.
signals.name: Correct limit with no sign argument
signals.observation: The limiting value is right and nothing says why solutions move toward it from the given start.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the rate exactly at the carrying capacity.
signals.name: Fastest change reported at the capacity
signals.observation: The response names the carrying capacity as the value at which the quantity changes fastest.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what each number measures and in what units.
signals.name: Two correct values with no interpretation
signals.observation: The capacity and the fastest change value are right and neither is read back into the situation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the same average on an interval of length one; a correct answer there and a wrong answer elsewhere points at the missing division rather than at the area reading.
signals.name: Geometric area read correctly with no division by the interval length
signals.observation: The response adds the triangle and rectangle areas under the graph correctly and reports that total as the average value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the integral on the subinterval below the axis alone; a positive answer there separates the sign reading from a counting slip in the grid.
signals.name: Signed area treated as unsigned when the graph dips below the axis
signals.observation: Every region under the graph is added as a positive area, so an interval where the function is negative raises the reported average.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different; a student who can answer had an omission rather than a missing idea.
signals.name: Average value named without units or without the interval
signals.observation: The sentence says what the average value is of but omits the units of the function or the interval it is taken over.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the divisor and of the integral separately, which separates a cancelling slip from a belief that the integral is already the average.
signals.name: Units built from the wrong factors
signals.observation: The units quoted are those of the integral, so the units of the independent variable are still carried in the reported average.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the integral on each side of the zero of velocity; correct signed pieces with a wrong total points at the splitting rather than at the integration.
signals.name: One integral over the whole interval with a single absolute value
signals.observation: Velocity is integrated across its sign change and the absolute value is applied once, at the end.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the times at which the velocity is zero on the interval; failure there places the gap in solving the equation, not in the accumulation idea.
signals.name: Sign change of velocity not located
signals.observation: No zero of velocity appears anywhere in the response, so no split is possible even though total distance is asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Give the same acceleration with two different initial velocities and ask for the later velocity in each case.
signals.name: Accumulated change reported as the velocity
signals.observation: The integral of acceleration is evaluated correctly and handed in as the velocity, with the initial velocity never added.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the numerical value of the integral alone, which separates a stalled evaluation from an incomplete structure.
signals.name: Velocity value left as an unevaluated setup
signals.observation: The sum of the initial velocity and the integral is written and no value is produced.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the net rate should be at a time when the two rates are equal.
signals.name: Net rate written as the sum of the two rates
signals.observation: The two given rates are added, so the net rate is largest when inflow and outflow are equal.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two named rates adds to the amount; a correct answer with a reversed expression points at the transcription.
signals.name: Difference taken in the wrong order
signals.observation: The outflow rate is written first, so the net rate has the wrong sign throughout.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which variable the integral is taken with respect to; a correct answer makes this a notation omission rather than a variable confusion.
signals.name: Integral expression written without its differential
signals.observation: The limits and the integrand are correct and the differential is missing from the expression.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the number the expression produces would mean in the context of the stem.
signals.name: Expression answers a different question than the one asked
signals.observation: The integral is set up for the change in the quantity where the amount present was requested, or over an interval the prompt did not name.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the unrounded intermediate value and for the final answer again; agreement then places the cause in the rounding step.
signals.name: Intermediate value rounded before the final computation
signals.observation: A rounded value from an earlier step is carried into the accumulation, so the reported amount disagrees in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the number would mean to someone reading the stem, which separates a missing sentence from a missing interpretation.
signals.name: Value reported with no statement of what it counts
signals.observation: A correct decimal appears with no sentence naming the quantity or the interval it applies to.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate both functions at one interior input and say which is larger.
signals.name: Difference of the boundary functions taken in the wrong order
signals.observation: The integrand is the lower curve minus the upper curve, so the area comes out negative and the sign is corrected only at the end.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the lower boundary of the region is at one interior input.
signals.name: Only one boundary curve placed in the integrand
signals.observation: The area is written as the integral of the upper curve alone, as though the region were bounded below by the horizontal axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many solutions the equation has on the interval; a correct count with a single limit points at the solving step.
signals.name: Intersection equation solved with one root lost
signals.observation: The equation setting the two curves equal is written correctly and only one of its solutions is carried into the limits.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two inputs bound the region and why.
signals.name: Limits taken from the graph window rather than from the boundary
signals.observation: The endpoints are the edges of the displayed viewing window, not the inputs at which the curves meet.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which variable the slices of the region run along, which separates the choice from the algebra of rewriting.
signals.name: Integration variable chosen against the shape of the region
signals.observation: The region is bounded left and right by curves given as x in terms of y, and the setup integrates in x with the boundaries unrewritten.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to solve the boundary equation for the other variable on its own.
signals.name: Boundary curve not solved for the other variable
signals.observation: The correct variable of integration is named and the curve is never rewritten, so the integrand keeps the wrong letter.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the integral would give if the two lobes had equal area.
signals.name: Absolute value bars omitted from the single integral form
signals.observation: The one integral form of the area is written with the difference exposed, so the two lobes cancel.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the integrand on each side of the crossing.
signals.name: Region treated as having one order of subtraction throughout
signals.observation: Neither bars nor a split appear, and one fixed order of subtraction runs across the crossing of the curves.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to mark one slice on the figure and label both of its ends.
signals.name: Slice side written as one function value
signals.observation: The side of the cross section is the upper curve alone although the region is bounded by two curves.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the length of the slice at one interior input as a number.
signals.name: Distance between the curves written in the wrong order
signals.observation: The side is a difference of the two curves taken so that it is negative on the interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of one slice with both dimensions labelled.
signals.name: Second dimension of the rectangle omitted
signals.observation: The rectangular section is squared as though the stated multiple relating height to base were one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what quantity the integrand has to carry for the integral to give a volume.
signals.name: Area of the slice replaced by its side
signals.observation: The integrand is the distance between the curves rather than the area of the rectangle built on it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to expand the expression for a specific pair of numbers and compare.
signals.name: Squared difference expanded incorrectly
signals.observation: The correct integrand is written and the expansion of the squared binomial loses the middle term or a sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value again from the unrounded setup; agreement places the cause in the rounding.
signals.name: Intermediate value rounded before the volume is reported
signals.observation: A rounded limit or coefficient is carried into the evaluation, so the reported volume disagrees in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a single equilateral triangle of a stated side length.
signals.name: Constant factor of the equilateral area missing
signals.observation: The integrand is the square of the side with no fractional constant in front.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area formula on its own, away from the integral.
signals.name: Area of the named shape not available
signals.observation: No area formula for the equilateral section appears anywhere, so the integrand is left as the side.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which side of the triangle lies in the base region.
signals.name: Stated distance used as a leg when it is the hypotenuse
signals.observation: The right isosceles section is given the leg formula although the distance between the curves lies along the hypotenuse.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a right isosceles triangle with a stated leg.
signals.name: Halving of the leg product omitted
