signals.observation: The correct leg is identified and the integrand is the square of the leg with no factor of one half.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and compare it with the formula just written.
signals.name: Correct area formula with the constant lost in the integral
signals.observation: The area of the named section is written correctly beside the integral and the constant does not appear inside it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the integral alone, which separates a stalled evaluation from an incomplete setup.
signals.name: Setup written with no value produced
signals.observation: The volume integral is complete and correct and no number is reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of one disc of a stated radius.
signals.name: Radius left unsquared in the disc integrand
signals.observation: The integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times the square of the function.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the area of a circular slice of that radius is.
signals.name: Factor of pi omitted from the disc integrand
signals.observation: The square of the radius is integrated correctly and the constant factor never appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the distance from one point on the curve to the stated line.
signals.name: Radius written as the bare function value about a shifted axis
signals.observation: The solid is revolved about a line other than an axis and the radius is the function value with no subtraction.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the curve lies above or below the axis of revolution on the interval.
signals.name: Subtraction for the shifted radius taken in the wrong order
signals.observation: The radius is written as the line minus the function where the curve lies farther from the axis, so the radius is negative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which inputs the region occupies, independently of where the axis is.
signals.name: Limits translated along with the axis
signals.observation: The endpoints of integration are shifted by the same amount as the line of revolution.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to mark the region on the figure and read its endpoints off the axis.
signals.name: Shift applied twice to the radius and once to the limits
signals.observation: The radius carries the correct subtraction and the endpoints carry it as well, so the interval no longer matches the region.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the length of a straight segment of slope one on an interval of length one should be.
signals.name: Length written as the integral of the derivative
signals.observation: The arc length integral is stated without the radical, so a segment of slope one on an interval of length one comes out as one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the formula gives for a horizontal segment, where the derivative is zero.
signals.name: Added one missing inside the radical
signals.observation: The radical is present and contains only the square of the derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the integrand for a linear function and compare it with the Pythagorean length.
signals.name: Derivative not squared inside the radical
signals.observation: The integrand is the square root of one plus the derivative itself.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two inputs the described piece of curve runs between.
signals.name: Limits taken from inputs the described curve does not occupy
signals.observation: The radical is correct and the interval of integration is not the one the description bounds.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
signals.name: Numerical length reported with no integral shown
signals.observation: A decimal for the arc length appears with no integral expression anywhere in the response.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value again from the written expression; agreement places the cause in the rounding.
signals.name: Value rounded early or stored from a truncated expression
signals.observation: The expression is correct and the reported value disagrees with it in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for each component derivative on its own before any quotient is formed.
signals.name: One component derivative computed incorrectly
signals.observation: One of dx/dt or dy/dt loses a chain rule factor, so every later quantity built from it is wrong.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which letter the two given equations have in common.
signals.name: Components differentiated with respect to the wrong variable
signals.observation: The derivative of y is taken with respect to x although both coordinates are given in the parameter.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the tangent line at a parameter value where dx/dt is zero.
signals.name: Slope formula applied where dx/dt vanishes
signals.observation: The quotient is evaluated at a parameter value at which the denominator is zero and a value is still reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask why the quotient is allowed at that parameter value.
signals.name: Condition never written although the work respects it
signals.observation: The parameter values used all have dx/dt nonzero and the condition is nowhere stated where the question asks for it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the coordinates of the particle at that time before the line is written.
signals.name: Tangent line written through the velocity components
signals.observation: The point in the line is the pair of derivative values rather than the coordinates of the particle.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line just written.
signals.name: Correct point and slope assembled into the wrong line form
signals.observation: The point and the slope are both right and the line is written with the coordinates exchanged.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the slope is when the numerator of the quotient is zero.
signals.name: Horizontal and vertical tangent conditions exchanged
signals.observation: The parameter values where dx/dt is zero are reported as giving horizontal tangents.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many solutions the equation has on the stated parameter interval.
signals.name: One solution of the tangent condition lost
signals.observation: The right condition is set to zero and only one of its parameter solutions is reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value again from the unrounded expression; agreement places the cause in the rounding.
signals.name: Second derivative evaluated from a rounded first derivative
signals.observation: The structure of the second derivative is right and a rounded intermediate value is substituted, so the value disagrees in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the expression that the calculator evaluated.
signals.name: Value reported with no expression for the second derivative
signals.observation: A correct decimal appears with nothing showing what was differentiated or divided.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity has to be positive for the curve in the plane to bend upward.
signals.name: Concavity read from the sign of a component derivative
signals.observation: The curve is called concave up because the second derivative of y with respect to the parameter is positive.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the expression at a parameter value inside the stated interval.
signals.name: Correct second derivative with its sign read at the wrong parameter value
signals.observation: The expression for the second derivative of y with respect to x is right and its sign is taken at a parameter value outside the interval asked about.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
signals.name: Length reported with no integral shown
signals.observation: A decimal for the parametric arc length appears with no integral expression anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value again from the written expression; agreement places the cause in the rounding.
signals.name: Value rounded before the length is reported
signals.observation: The integral is written correctly and the reported value disagrees with it in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which parameter values the path returns to a point it has already visited.
signals.name: Interval chosen so that the path is traced more than once
signals.observation: The length is computed over a parameter interval that covers part of the path twice.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to underline the parameter interval in the stem before writing the limits.
signals.name: Interval copied from another part of the question
signals.observation: The integrand is correct and the limits are those of the previous part rather than those the stem names.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two numbers is the rate in the horizontal direction.
signals.name: Components given with no labels or in the order they were computed
signals.observation: Two correct numbers appear with no indication of which is horizontal and which vertical.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the second component on its own.
signals.name: One component differentiated and the other copied
signals.observation: The derivative of one component is right and the other component is reproduced undifferentiated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to underline the time the stem names before substituting.
signals.name: Velocity components evaluated at the wrong time
signals.observation: The derivative expressions are correct and the substituted time is one from an earlier part.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the later value again from the unrounded components.
signals.name: Rounded components carried into a later part
signals.observation: The components are rounded before the speed or the position is built from them, so the later value disagrees in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which component belongs to which coordinate.
signals.name: Vector notation dropped when the components are listed
signals.observation: The two component functions are written as a bare pair with no vector notation and no labels.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the horizontal coordinate of the particle at one time from each of the two forms.
signals.name: Components exchanged in the conversion
signals.observation: The parametric pair is rewritten in vector form with the horizontal and vertical components swapped.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many conditions the initial position supplies.
signals.name: One constant of integration used for both components
signals.observation: The vector antiderivative carries a single constant rather than one in each component.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the antiderivative of the second component on its own.
signals.name: One component antidifferentiated correctly and the other left as given
signals.observation: The first component is integrated and the second is copied unchanged into the position vector.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for both Cartesian coordinates of the point at a stated angle.
signals.name: Polar radius written as a Cartesian coordinate
signals.observation: The value of r is placed on the x line or the y line of the answer.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the vertical coordinate on its own.
signals.name: One conversion formula applied and the other omitted
signals.observation: The horizontal coordinate is converted correctly and the vertical coordinate is left as r or as the angle.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what quantity r measures before the derivative is interpreted.
signals.name: Derivative of r described as the speed along the curve
signals.observation: The interpretation sentence names the speed of the particle rather than the rate at which its distance from the origin changes.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two points the distance in the sentence runs between.
signals.name: Sentence omits what the distance is measured from
signals.observation: The rate is called a rate of change of distance with no mention of the origin or of the angle it is taken with respect to.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the units of the requested rate are.
signals.name: Rate in time reported as dr/dtheta alone
signals.observation: The chain rule product is written without the rate at which the angle changes.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which time each factor is evaluated.
signals.name: Product formed with the angle rate at the wrong instant
signals.observation: Both factors appear and the rate of the angle is substituted at a time other than the one asked about.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the slope of the tangent to a circle of constant radius, where dr/dtheta is zero.
signals.name: Slope of the polar curve reported as dr/dtheta
signals.observation: The derivative of r is handed in where the slope of the tangent line in the plane was requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name the two factors in that coordinate before differentiating.
signals.name: Product rule omitted in one of the two coordinates
signals.observation: The Cartesian coordinates are formed correctly and one of them is differentiated as a single factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which angles the two curves meet.
signals.name: Bounding angles taken from the figure rather than the intersection
signals.observation: The angle interval runs across the whole drawn figure instead of between the angles at which the curves meet.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many solutions the equation setting the radii equal has on the interval.
signals.name: One bounding angle found and the other assumed
signals.observation: One intersection angle is solved for and the second limit is taken from the stem without being checked.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which angles r returns to zero.
signals.name: Angle interval covers the loop more than once
signals.observation: The interval runs over a full revolution although the loop closes on a shorter interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the angles at which r is zero on their own, away from the integral.
signals.name: Angles where r is zero not located
signals.observation: No solution of r equal to zero appears, so the loop is never delimited.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
signals.name: Area reported with no integral shown
signals.observation: A decimal for the polar area appears with no integral expression anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value again from the written expression.
signals.name: Value rounded before the area is reported
signals.observation: The integral is correct and the reported value disagrees with it in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve is farther from the origin at an angle inside the interval.
signals.name: Outer and inner radii exchanged in the integrand
signals.observation: The square of the nearer curve is subtracted from the square of the farther one in the wrong order, giving a negative integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two radii at an angle on each side of their intersection.
signals.name: Outer curve decided once for the whole figure
signals.observation: One curve is treated as outer across an interval on which the two curves exchange places.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to read the chain of equalities aloud and check each link.
signals.name: Variable expression equated to the numerical area
signals.observation: The integral expression and its value are joined by an equals sign to a third quantity that is not equal to either.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the difference again from the unrounded values.
signals.name: Value rounded before the difference of the two areas is taken
signals.observation: Each polar area is rounded and then subtracted, so the reported difference disagrees in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which part of the region the integral just written covers.
signals.name: Symmetry used without the compensating factor
signals.observation: Half of a symmetric region is integrated and the result is reported without doubling.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask over which angles the integral already runs before the factor is applied.
signals.name: Doubling applied to a region that was already whole
signals.observation: The integral runs over the full region and the result is doubled as well.

signals.distinguish_by: A learner who repairs the wording once asked what the vertical axis measures is partial_conceptual; one who cannot is a prerequisite gap in reading rate notation.
signals.name: Quantity named while the rate is described as an amount
signals.observation: The sentence names the accumulated quantity but calls the plotted values amounts present rather than a rate per unit input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sentence directly; producing it on request places the learner at notation_only rather than partial_conceptual.
signals.name: Correct area computed with no interpreting sentence
signals.observation: The signed area is evaluated correctly and the response stops at the number, with no statement of what accumulated over which interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of one Riemann sum term; correct product units there show the rule is known and the transfer failed.
signals.name: Rate units reported as accumulation units
signals.observation: The units given are the units of the plotted rate rather than the product of rate units and input units.

signals.distinguish_by: Vary the input units in a second prompt; a learner reproducing the product rather than a memorised phrase is mastered.
signals.name: Units stated as a product with the interval named
signals.observation: Units are given as rate units times input units and the interval of accumulation appears in the same sentence.

signals.distinguish_by: Give a rate that is positive but decreasing; calling the change negative there is partial_conceptual rather than a reading slip.
signals.name: Sign of the change read from the sign of the quantity
signals.observation: The response says the quantity fell because the graph lies low on the axis rather than because the rate is negative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign on each piece separately; correct pieces with a wrong total locates the failure at the combination step.
signals.name: Sign decided correctly on one interval and not across a sign change
signals.observation: The direction is right where the rate keeps one sign and is asserted from the last piece alone when the rate changes sign inside the interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the piece below the axis alone; a correct sign there makes the failure an assembly step, not BC-MIS-08024.
signals.name: Pieces computed correctly and added as magnitudes
signals.observation: Triangle and rectangle areas are right and every piece is added positively, so a region below the axis raises the total.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a single labelled piece with no integral present; a wrong formula there is a prerequisite gap rather than an integration failure.
signals.name: Area formulas recalled without their constant factors
signals.observation: A triangular piece is given base times height, or a semicircular piece the area of the full circle.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which input each height belongs to; naming the centres correctly while using endpoints marks a procedural slip.
signals.name: Midpoint values read at the subinterval endpoints
signals.observation: The widths are right and the heights are taken from the tabulated endpoints rather than from the centres.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the answer is above or below the integral and why; an inability to say either points to BC-MIS-06003.
signals.name: Midpoint sum treated as exact
signals.observation: The midpoint value is reported as the value of the integral with no statement that it is an approximation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the function value at one named input; a correct value there separates figure reading from the sum structure.
signals.name: Heights read off the graph at the wrong gridline
signals.observation: The sum has the right structure and one or more heights are taken from a neighbouring gridline of the figure.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of one term; rate units alone are consistent with BC-MIS-06001.
signals.name: Values added with no width supplied when none is tabulated
signals.observation: With a formula or a graph rather than a table, the response adds function values and never forms a width.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the symbol outside the function stands for; naming it as a width while omitting it is notation_only.
signals.name: Sigma expression expanded without the width factor
signals.observation: The terms are written out in the right order and each is a function value with no width attached.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many terms the sum has before any term is written.
signals.name: Index range expanded with one term too many or too few
signals.observation: The expansion starts or stops one index off, so the first or last term of the sum is wrong.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what one subinterval measures when the count doubles.
signals.name: Width written as the interval length rather than as its quotient
signals.observation: The sigma expression uses the full interval length in place of the length divided by the number of subintervals.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to write the second term explicitly; a correct second term marks a notation failure.
signals.name: Sample point written without reference to the index
signals.observation: The function is evaluated at a fixed endpoint inside the sigma, so every term repeats.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity in the limit expression carries the interval; naming it correctly points away from BC-MIS-06001.
signals.name: Limits of integration read from the index range
signals.observation: The integral is written from one to the number of subintervals rather than from the endpoints of the interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the sample point approaches as the number of subintervals grows.
signals.name: Integrand kept in the sample point form
signals.observation: The integrand is written with the index expression still in it rather than in the variable of integration.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to one subinterval as the count grows.
signals.name: Limit written with the width fixed
signals.observation: The sum is produced correctly and the limit is taken over the number of terms with the width left constant.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the written sum equals the integral or approximates it.
signals.name: Sum written correctly and the limit symbol omitted
signals.observation: The sigma expression matches the integral term by term and no limit is written in front of it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether a partition with one wide piece and many narrow ones satisfies the definition.
signals.name: Definition stated without the widths going to zero
signals.observation: The statement names a limit of sums as the number of subintervals grows and never constrains the subinterval widths.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the choice of sample point changes the limit.
signals.name: Definition recited with the sample point unquantified
signals.observation: The definition is reproduced and nothing is said about where in each subinterval the function is evaluated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which letter varies when the function is evaluated at two inputs.
signals.name: Upper limit and variable of integration written with the same letter
signals.observation: The accumulation function is written with x in both the upper limit and the integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the written function gives at the stated starting input; a nonzero value exposes the wrong lower limit.
signals.name: Lower limit taken from the wrong point of the stem
signals.observation: The integral starts at the input asked about rather than at the stated starting input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the upper limit on its own; a correct factor there makes the omission procedural.
signals.name: Derivative reported as the integrand with the chain rule factor missing
signals.observation: With a composite upper limit the answer is the integrand evaluated there and no derivative of the limit appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the derivative gives at one numerical input.
signals.name: Derivative written in the variable of integration
signals.observation: The answer is left in the dummy variable, so the result is not a function of the independent variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value at the starting input; anything other than zero exposes the wrong origin of accumulation.
signals.name: Signed area accumulated from the wrong starting point
signals.observation: The geometry is right and the running total begins at the left edge of the figure rather than at the stated lower limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the plotted curve is called in the stem before any value is read.
signals.name: Plotted values read as values of the accumulation function
signals.observation: The value reported at an input is the height of the plotted curve there rather than the area up to it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must be true of the integrand before the theorem may be used; a correct statement on request is a reporting gap.
signals.name: Theorem applied with no hypothesis stated
signals.observation: The derivative of the accumulation function is written down and continuity of the integrand is never mentioned.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two functions the theorem assumes continuous.
signals.name: Hypothesis stated about the wrong function
signals.observation: Continuity is claimed for the accumulation function rather than for the integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the sign of the plotted values means for the accumulation; monotonicity language about the wrong function points to BC-MIS-05011.
signals.name: Intervals of increase read from where the plotted curve rises
signals.observation: The response says the accumulation function increases where the plotted curve rises rather than where it is above the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the plotted curve crosses the axis before the interval is written.
signals.name: Sign of the integrand read correctly and the endpoints of the interval misreported
signals.observation: The right regions are identified and the reported interval endpoints are off by one gridline.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the slope of the plotted curve controls; naming the second derivative there separates the two rules.
signals.name: Concavity decided from the sign of the integrand
signals.observation: The response says the accumulation function is concave up where the plotted curve is above the axis.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what feature of the plotted curve makes the claim true.
signals.name: Concavity right and the supporting reason stated only about the accumulation function
signals.observation: The intervals are correct and the justification restates that the accumulation function changes concavity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask separately where the accumulation function bends up; a correct answer on request marks an incomplete report.
signals.name: Description correct in monotonicity and silent on concavity
signals.observation: Intervals of increase and decrease are right and no statement about bending appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function the stem plots before any feature is located.
signals.name: Features of the plotted curve transcribed as features of the accumulation function
signals.observation: Extrema and inflection points of the accumulation function are placed at the visible extrema and inflection points of the plotted curve.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two integrals written separately before any value is substituted.
signals.name: Constant pulled out of only one term of a sum
signals.observation: The integral of a sum is split correctly and a constant factor is kept inside one of the resulting integrals.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the split can be checked by differentiating the result.
signals.name: A product treated the way a sum is treated
signals.observation: The integral of a product is split into a product of integrals by analogy with the sum property.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the two integrals add to.
signals.name: Limits swapped without the sign change
signals.observation: The reversed integral is reported with the same value as the original.

signals.distinguish_by: Give three overlapping given values; combining them without prompting is mastered rather than rule recall.
signals.name: Reversal used deliberately to align adjacent intervals
signals.observation: The limits are reversed with the sign changed in order to join two given integrals over touching intervals.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which interval the difference covers.
signals.name: Adjacent intervals combined with a subtraction reversed
signals.observation: The pieces are the right ones and the given values are subtracted in the wrong order.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each piece is finite before they are added.
signals.name: Property applied across a point where the integrand is undefined
signals.observation: Two intervals are joined although the integrand is unbounded at the shared endpoint.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what width the sum has when the two limits agree.
signals.name: Degenerate integral given the value of the integrand
signals.observation: The integral from a point to itself is reported as the value of the integrand at that point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the accumulation function at its starting input.
signals.name: Degenerate case used to fix a constant of accumulation
signals.observation: The zero value at the starting input is used to state the accumulation function there.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the integrand is continuous before the setup is written.
signals.name: Single antiderivative carried across a jump
signals.observation: One expression is antidifferentiated over the whole interval although the definition changes inside it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which branch applies on each piece before either is evaluated.
signals.name: Interval split correctly and one piece evaluated with the other branch
signals.observation: The split point is right and one of the two pieces uses the formula belonging to the other piece.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the sign of the integral should be from the graph before the subtraction is read.
signals.name: Endpoints substituted in the wrong order
signals.observation: A correct antiderivative is evaluated as the lower value minus the upper value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the integrand at one input and compare with a hand estimate; disagreement isolates the tool state.
signals.name: Antiderivative correct and the result reported from a calculator in the wrong angle mode
signals.observation: The symbolic work is right and the numerical value of a trigonometric integrand does not match a hand estimate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the theorem assumes before it is used.
signals.name: Conclusion used with no continuity hypothesis named
signals.observation: The difference of antiderivative values is applied to an integrand with a jump inside the interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function is evaluated at the two limits.
signals.name: Hypotheses listed and the conclusion stated about the integrand
signals.observation: The statement names the right conditions and then asserts the conclusion about the integrand rather than about an antiderivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the integral alone measures before the final value is requested.
signals.name: Integral of the rate reported as the amount present
signals.observation: The value of the integral is given as the quantity at the later input, with no starting value added.

signals.distinguish_by: Compare the integrand at one input with a hand estimate.
signals.name: Correct setup evaluated with the calculator in degree mode
signals.observation: The integral is set up correctly and a trigonometric rate is evaluated in degree mode.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the difference of the two rates measures at one instant.
signals.name: Two integrals written where one difference was asked for
signals.observation: Inflow and outflow are integrated separately and the results are added rather than differenced.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the model predicts when the outflow rate exceeds the inflow rate.
signals.name: Net rate assembled with the outflow sign lost
signals.observation: The single integral is written with the two rates added, so the quantity never decreases.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the result and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Exponent raised without the matching division
signals.observation: The power is increased by one and the new exponent does not appear as a divisor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the expression rewritten as a power before any antidifferentiation.
signals.name: Radicals and reciprocals left unconverted
signals.observation: The rule is applied correctly to visible powers and not to a root or a reciprocal in the same integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which exponent the power rule cannot handle.
signals.name: Reciprocal integrand sent through the power rule
signals.observation: The integrand with exponent negative one is raised to exponent zero and divided by zero or reported as a constant.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the result and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Exponential antiderivative written without its inner constant
signals.observation: The exponential form is recognised and the constant from the exponent does not appear as a divisor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the reported answer.
signals.name: Sign of a trigonometric antiderivative reversed
signals.observation: The correct pair of functions is used and the sign is the opposite of the one the derivative rule gives.

signals.distinguish_by: Compare one evaluated value with a hand estimate.
signals.name: Correct antiderivative evaluated in degree mode
signals.observation: The symbolic antiderivative is right and the numerical evaluation disagrees with a hand estimate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which standard form the integrand matches term by term.
signals.name: Inverse trigonometric form matched on the denominator alone
signals.observation: An integrand with a squared term in the denominator is sent to the inverse tangent form although the structure does not match.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the reported answer.
signals.name: Correct form used with the constant inside the root mishandled
signals.observation: The right inverse trigonometric family is chosen and the constant is not factored out before the form is applied.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the answer would be if a value of the antiderivative at one input were different.
signals.name: Antiderivative reported as a single function
signals.observation: The indefinite integral is written with no constant and treated as the unique answer.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the reported function gives at the supplied input.
signals.name: Constant written and never determined
signals.observation: The constant appears and the supplied initial value is not used to solve for it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the inner expression on its own.
signals.name: Candidate differentiated with the chain rule factor dropped
signals.observation: The verification differentiates the candidate and loses the inner derivative, so the check appears to succeed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what operation turns a candidate back into the integrand.
signals.name: Verification replaced by a comparison of shapes
signals.observation: The candidate is declared an antiderivative because it resembles the integrand, with no derivative taken.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the written form and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Elementary antiderivative invented for a non elementary integrand
signals.observation: A closed form is written for an integrand that has none, usually by antidifferentiating the outer function alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which expression the numerical value came from.
signals.name: Recognition correct and the integral form abandoned
signals.observation: The learner says no antiderivative is available and then reports a numerical value with no integral written.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to write du and point to it inside the integrand.
signals.name: Inner function chosen from the composite alone
signals.observation: A substitution is set up for the inside of a composite although no constant multiple of its derivative appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the reported antiderivative.
signals.name: Inner function chosen correctly and the constant from du dropped
signals.observation: The substitution is right and the reciprocal constant that du introduces is missing from the result.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the answer gives at one numerical input of the original variable.
signals.name: Answer left in the substituted variable
signals.observation: The antiderivative is correct and is reported in u with no return to the original variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether any u remains in the final line.
signals.name: Back substitution made into part of the expression only
signals.observation: The substituted variable is replaced in one term and left standing in another.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the two limits mean for the substituted variable.
signals.name: Original limits substituted into an expression in the substituted variable
signals.observation: The antiderivative stays in u and the original limits are substituted into it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which variable the written limits belong to at each line.
signals.name: Back substitution done and one limit converted as well
signals.observation: The expression is returned to the original variable and one of the limits is converted a second time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the reported answer.
signals.name: Logarithm written without the constant from the numerator
signals.observation: The derivative over function pattern is recognised and the constant multiple is not carried through.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the denominator and compare with the numerator.
signals.name: Pattern claimed where the numerator is not the derivative
signals.observation: A logarithm is written although the numerator is not a constant multiple of the derivative of the denominator.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two degrees before anything is written.
signals.name: Decomposition begun without a degree comparison
signals.observation: An integrand whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree is split into partial fractions directly.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to multiply the result back out and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Division performed with the remainder mishandled
signals.observation: The quotient is correct and the remainder term is dropped or left over the wrong denominator.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to expand the rewritten form and compare with the original quadratic.
signals.name: Square completed with the constant not balanced
signals.observation: The quadratic is rewritten as a square and the compensating constant is omitted or has the wrong sign.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which standard form the rewritten integrand now matches.
signals.name: Completed square not carried into a standard form
signals.observation: The rewriting is correct and no inverse trigonometric or logarithmic form is identified from it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to recombine the split terms over one denominator.
signals.name: Single fraction split across the numerator only
signals.observation: The numerator is broken into terms and one of the resulting terms keeps the whole original denominator plus an extra factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to test the split at one numerical input.
signals.name: Denominator split term by term
signals.observation: A single fraction with a sum in the denominator is written as a sum of two fractions.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which structural feature the chosen technique requires and where it appears here.
signals.name: Technique chosen from the surface look of the integrand
signals.observation: Substitution is started on a rational integrand because a denominator is present, with no check of degrees or factors.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to state the first line of the technique they named.
signals.name: Correct choice named and the other route carried out
signals.observation: The learner says division is needed and then decomposes, or names substitution and rearranges instead.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the result and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Product antidifferentiated factor by factor
signals.observation: Each factor of the product is antidifferentiated and the results are multiplied.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two factors becomes simpler when differentiated.
signals.name: Parts set up with the assignment reversed
signals.observation: The factor that simplifies under differentiation is assigned to dv, so the new integral is harder than the original.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to derive the parts formula from the product rule and compare with each line.
signals.name: Sign lost on the second application
signals.observation: The first application is correct and the minus sign in front of the remaining integral is dropped the second time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the second application produced and whether it is simpler than the first integral.
signals.name: Second application made with the roles swapped
signals.observation: The second use of parts assigns the roles the other way round, returning the original integral.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the product term at each limit.
signals.name: Boundary term left unevaluated
signals.observation: The parts expression is correct and the product term is carried as an expression rather than evaluated at both limits.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which parts of the line the limits apply to.
signals.name: Limits applied to the remaining integral only
signals.observation: The limits are substituted into the leftover integral and not into the product term.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which values of the unknown function the stem actually supplies.
signals.name: Unknown function antidifferentiated by name
signals.observation: The response writes an antiderivative symbol for the unknown function and treats it as a supplied value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which input each supplied value belongs to.
signals.name: Parts applied correctly and the supplied values misassigned
signals.observation: The parts expression is right and the tabulated values are substituted at the wrong limits.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the roots of the denominator before any decomposition.
signals.name: Denominator left unfactored
signals.observation: The decomposition is attempted over the quadratic denominator as written.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to multiply the factors back out.
signals.name: Factors found with a sign reversed
signals.observation: The denominator is factored and one factor carries the wrong sign, so the later constants come out negated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to test the identity at one numerical input.
signals.name: Denominators cleared and one term omitted
signals.observation: The equation for the constants is set up and one of the products is dropped when the identity is expanded.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what equation the constants are supposed to satisfy.
signals.name: Constants read off without clearing denominators
signals.observation: The numerators are assigned by inspection from the original numerator with no identity solved.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the derivative of the reported antiderivative.
signals.name: Logarithms written without their constant multiples
signals.observation: Each simple fraction becomes a logarithm and the numerator constants do not appear in front.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to test the combined form at one numerical input.
signals.name: Logarithm of the sum written for the sum of logarithms
signals.observation: The two logarithms are combined into one logarithm of a sum.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of each term at each limit.
signals.name: Decomposition correct and the limits substituted into one term
signals.observation: Both logarithmic terms are right and the limits are applied to only one of them.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the integrand is undefined before the limits are used.
signals.name: Integral evaluated across a root of the denominator
signals.observation: The limits straddle an input where the denominator vanishes and the integral is evaluated as if it were proper.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the integrand is unbounded on the closed interval.
signals.name: Impropriety at an unbounded integrand overlooked
signals.observation: An infinite limit of integration is named as the cause and an interior input where the integrand is unbounded is not.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the integrand near each endpoint.
signals.name: Cause named correctly and the wrong endpoint cited
signals.observation: The integral is called improper for the right reason and the endpoint identified is the one where nothing goes wrong.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which expression the limit is taken of and what variable approaches what.
signals.name: Infinite limit substituted in place of a limit
signals.observation: A correct antiderivative is evaluated by substituting the infinite endpoint directly.

signals.distinguish_by: Give a decaying integrand whose integral diverges and ask for the value.
signals.name: Convergence assumed from a decaying integrand
signals.observation: A finite value is reported because the integrand tends to zero, with no limit evaluated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the antiderivative does as the endpoint grows without bound.
signals.name: Finite value reported for a divergent integral
signals.observation: The limit is infinite and a number is reported, usually the value of the finite endpoint term alone.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the integral has a value or fails to have one.
signals.name: Divergence recognised and reported as a numerical answer
signals.observation: The learner says the limit is infinite and then writes infinity as the value of the integral.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many places on the interval make the integral improper.
signals.name: Interval split at the wrong place
signals.observation: The integral is broken into pieces and one piece still carries two sources of impropriety.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each piece converges before the pieces are combined.
signals.name: Pieces combined although one diverges
signals.observation: One piece diverges and the pieces are added to give a finite value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which structural feature the named technique requires and where it appears here.
signals.name: Technique named from the outer form of the integrand
signals.observation: Substitution is named because the integrand is a composite, with no check that the inner derivative appears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to write the first line of the technique they named.
signals.name: Technique named correctly and a different one carried out
signals.observation: The classification is right and the first written line belongs to another technique.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which precondition fails and what would have to appear for it to hold.
signals.name: Technique ruled out by appearance rather than by structure
signals.observation: Substitution is dismissed because the integrand is a product, with no reference to the missing inner derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the missing feature by name.
signals.name: Correct rejection stated with no reason
signals.observation: The response says the technique does not apply and gives no feature of the integrand.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what technique the remaining integral now calls for.
signals.name: First technique applied and the remaining integral abandoned
signals.observation: The substitution or the parts step is carried out correctly and the leftover integral is left unevaluated.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which expression the second step operates on.
signals.name: Second technique applied to the original integrand
signals.observation: The second step is applied to the integral as first written rather than to what the first step produced.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the learner to differentiate the written form and compare with the integrand.
signals.name: Closed form forced where none exists
signals.observation: An elementary antiderivative is written for an integrand that has none rather than leaving the integral form.

signals.distinguish_by: Compare the integrand at one input with a hand estimate.
signals.name: Integral form kept and the numerical value taken in degree mode
signals.observation: The definite integral is left in place and evaluated numerically with the calculator in the wrong angle mode.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the reported number; a rate answer without the division carries the units of the quantity.
signals.name: Interval change reported without the division
signals.observation: The two function values are subtracted correctly and the difference is reported as the average rate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask over which interval the number was computed; a correct interval with a wrong label separates procedure from interpretation.
signals.name: Average rate computed and then labelled as a rate at a point
signals.observation: The quotient is formed correctly over the interval and the answer sentence attaches it to one endpoint.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the denominator equals when the endpoints coincide, then ask whether that division is permitted.
signals.name: Zero length interval treated as an admissible case
signals.observation: The response computes the quotient with equal endpoints and reports zero rather than saying the quotient is undefined.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which part of the quotient fails; naming the denominator separates a learned phrase from the reason.
signals.name: Undefined quotient asserted with no reference to the denominator
signals.observation: The response says the average rate does not exist at a point but never names the vanishing denominator.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens to the average rates as the interval keeps shrinking, and whether the answer is one of them.
signals.name: Limit language absent from the description of the instantaneous rate
signals.observation: The response describes the rate at an instant as the rate over a very small interval, with no limit taken.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to read the expression under the limit symbol aloud and say what it measures.
signals.name: Correct limit statement with the wrong quantity inside
signals.observation: The limit notation is written correctly but the expression under it is the change in the function rather than the quotient.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask from which side the description says the inputs come, and where that appears in the written symbols.
signals.name: Approach direction omitted from the written limit
signals.observation: The described one sided approach is written as a two sided limit statement.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which number the inputs approach and which the outputs approach, then ask where each belongs.
signals.name: Target value and limit value exchanged in the notation
signals.observation: The input the variable approaches is written on the right of the equals sign and the limit value under the arrow.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the statement would still hold if the function were undefined at that input.
signals.name: Limit statement read as a claim about the value at the point
signals.observation: The written limit is described in words as saying what the function equals at the input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the function must ever take the limit value for the statement to be true.
signals.name: Limit statement read as an eventual arrival
signals.observation: The description says the function reaches the value once the input is close enough.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which inputs are smaller than the target, and which superscript records that set.
signals.name: One sided notation written with the sides exchanged
signals.observation: The superscript marking the side is attached so that the left hand approach is written as the right hand one.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the other side does, and whether the response examined it.
signals.name: Two sided statement written where only one side is supported
signals.observation: The response drops the side marker and claims a two sided limit from evidence on one side only.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the plotted value and the approached height as two separate questions.
signals.name: Filled point read in place of the approached height
signals.observation: The plotted value at the input is reported although the curve approaches a different height from both sides.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must hold between the two heights for the two sided limit to exist.
signals.name: Both one sided heights read correctly with no comparison made
signals.observation: The two approached heights are reported correctly and one of them is then named as the two sided limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value approached from the other side and whether the graph was traced on that side.
signals.name: Only the visible side of the graph read
signals.observation: One one sided value is reported correctly and the other is left blank or copied from the first.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the branch does just before the input, with the point at the input covered up.
signals.name: One sided value taken at the plotted point rather than along the approach
signals.observation: The one sided value reported is the height of the filled dot rather than the height the branch heads towards.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the symbol written names a real number, and what existence of a limit requires.
signals.name: Unbounded behaviour written as an existing limit
signals.observation: The response writes that the limit equals infinity and then calls the limit existing.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the behaviour on each side separately before the conclusion is stated.
signals.name: Unboundedness recognised on one side only
signals.observation: The growth is described correctly on one side and the other side is not examined before the conclusion is written.

signals.distinguish_by: Supply inputs spaced differently and ask whether the sampled outputs still agree.
signals.name: Oscillating values sampled into a single reported limit
signals.observation: One of the values the function swings between is reported as the limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the function values do as the inputs close in, and whether the answer names any pattern.
signals.name: Nonexistence asserted with no description of the swinging
signals.observation: The response says the limit does not exist but gives no account of the behaviour near the input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what a window ten times narrower would show, and whether the conclusion would survive it.
signals.name: Graph window treated as the whole story
signals.observation: The response reports a limit from one displayed window without noting what a narrower window could reveal.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the stated concern changes the confidence in the reported value.
signals.name: Scale concern stated with no consequence drawn
signals.observation: The response says the scale could mislead but still reports the reading as settled.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the outputs would do in a row closer to the target than any supplied.
signals.name: Last table row reported as the limit
signals.observation: The output in the final row is copied as the limit rather than the value the outputs crowd towards.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rows lie on each side of the target and whether both groups were used.
signals.name: Rows from one side only used for a two sided estimate
signals.observation: The estimate is built from the rows above the target while the rows below are ignored.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rows satisfy the side condition named in the question.
signals.name: Rows from both sides used for a one sided estimate
signals.observation: The one sided value is computed from rows lying on both sides of the target input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to restate the question and check the notation against it.
signals.name: Side marker ignored in the written answer
signals.observation: The correct rows are used and the answer is written without the side marker the question asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the function could do between the tabulated inputs, and whether the table rules that out.
signals.name: Agreement of decimals treated as settling the limit
signals.observation: The response calls the limit established because several tabulated outputs agree to the printed places.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether a table can establish nonexistence, and what else would be needed.
signals.name: Inconclusive table read as showing nonexistence
signals.observation: The response concludes that no limit exists because the tabulated outputs do not agree.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the limit of each part separately and whether both are finite.
signals.name: Sum theorem applied where one part has no limit
signals.observation: The limits are split across the sum although one of the two parts is unbounded near the input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which theorem permits the step just taken.
signals.name: Split written without the theorem being named
signals.observation: The splitting step is carried out correctly and no justification is offered when one is requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate the same limit with the constant written outside and compare.
signals.name: Constant left inside the limit and then dropped
signals.observation: The constant factor is not pulled out and does not appear in the final value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each factor has a limit before the product is taken.
signals.name: Product theorem applied to a factor with no limit
signals.observation: The limits are multiplied although one factor oscillates without settling.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the denominator limit on its own and what the theorem requires of it.
signals.name: Quotient theorem applied without the denominator check
signals.observation: The two limits are divided although the denominator limit is zero.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the numerator limit is, and whether the pair of values settles the question.
signals.name: Denominator check made and the zero case left unresolved
signals.observation: The response notes that the denominator limit is zero and concludes the limit does not exist.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the function has a value at the input before the substitution is made.
signals.name: Substitution used where the function is not continuous at the input
signals.observation: The target input is substituted into an expression that is undefined there and the result is reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the substitution gave, and whether further work could change a defined value.
signals.name: Rewriting continued after substitution already settles the limit
signals.observation: A legitimate direct value is obtained and the response keeps manipulating the expression and loses it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which function is applied first when the composite is evaluated at an ordinary input.
signals.name: Composite evaluated from the outside in
signals.observation: The limit of the outer function is taken first and the inner function is applied to that value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the outer function does at the value the inner one approaches.
signals.name: Composite theorem applied with no continuity check on the outer function
signals.observation: The inner limit is substituted into the outer function although the outer function breaks at that value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which branch governs inputs just below the boundary and which governs those just above.
signals.name: Boundary input substituted into the branch that does not apply
signals.observation: One of the two one sided values is computed from the wrong branch of the rule.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must hold between the two values before a two sided limit may be claimed.
signals.name: One sided values computed correctly with no comparison written
signals.observation: Both branch values are correct and the response names one of them as the two sided limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate both forms at an input near the target and compare the two numbers.
signals.name: Conjugate applied to one part of the expression only
signals.observation: The numerator is multiplied by the conjugate and the denominator is left unchanged.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what remains to be done once the common factor has been divided out.
signals.name: Conjugate step completed and the substitution never made
signals.observation: The radical is cleared and the response stops before the target input is substituted.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check the cancellation numerically at one convenient input.
signals.name: Summand cancelled from a complex fraction
signals.observation: A matching term in the numerator and the denominator is divided out although it is not a factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what substitution gives in the cleared expression.
signals.name: Nested fraction cleared and the form not reclassified
signals.observation: The nesting is cleared correctly and the response still reports the limit as indeterminate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which identity would remove the vanishing factor rather than only rewriting the expression.
signals.name: Identity applied that leaves the indeterminate form unchanged
signals.observation: A correct identity is used and the rewritten expression still gives zero over zero under substitution.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to test the identity at one convenient input.
signals.name: Identity misremembered so the rewritten expression is not equal
signals.observation: The rewriting changes the value of the expression, and the reported limit follows from the changed form.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the numerator and the denominator each approach, and whether the pair determines the quotient.
signals.name: Form named as a value rather than as indeterminate
signals.observation: Substitution gives zero over zero and the response records zero as the limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the numerator limit, then ask whether the two cases call for the same conclusion.
signals.name: Zero over zero and nonzero over zero not distinguished
signals.observation: The response treats every vanishing denominator as the same case and reports nonexistence.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what feature of the expression decides between the two methods.
signals.name: Factoring attempted on a form that calls for a conjugate
signals.observation: A radical expression is attacked by factoring, and when that fails the response reports nonexistence.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the first step is for any limit expression, before any method is chosen.
signals.name: Method chosen before the form under substitution is named
signals.observation: The rewriting begins with no substitution test, and a limit that direct substitution settles is rewritten instead.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what substitution gave and whether anything about that value needed repair.
signals.name: Legitimate direct value discarded in favour of more rewriting
signals.observation: Substitution gives a defined value and the response continues to manipulate the expression.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the expression has a value at the input before the answer is accepted.
signals.name: Direct value accepted where the expression is undefined at the input
signals.observation: The response stops at substitution although the denominator vanishes there.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must be true of the two bounding functions at the target input.
signals.name: Hypotheses stated as a single inequality with no limit condition
signals.observation: The bounding inequality is named and the requirement that the two bounds share a limit is left out.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to list the conditions before the conclusion is written.
signals.name: Theorem named with its hypotheses left unstated
signals.observation: The response names the theorem and moves to the conclusion without listing what it requires.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to test the inequality at one input on each side of the target.
signals.name: Inequality multiplied by a sign changing factor without reversal
signals.observation: The bounding inequality is multiplied through by a factor that is negative on one side and the inequality signs are left unchanged.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask on what interval around the point the inequality was checked.
signals.name: Bounding inequality asserted with no interval named
signals.observation: The response claims the function sits between the bounds without saying where that holds.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the next line of the argument does with the inequality just written.
signals.name: Oscillating factor bounded but the product never formed
signals.observation: The bounded factor is enclosed between negative one and one and the remaining factor is never multiplied through the inequality.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the multiplying factor on each side of the target input.
signals.name: Bounds multiplied without attention to the sign of the factor
signals.observation: The inequality is multiplied by a factor that changes sign at the target and the inequality signs are kept as written.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what each presentation says about the behaviour on each side of the input.
signals.name: Three presentations compared only by the value reported
signals.observation: The graph, the table, and the expression are said to agree because each yields the same number, with no side or asymptote behaviour compared.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the infinity symbol sits in each statement, under the arrow or after the equals sign.
signals.name: End behaviour statement matched with a statement about a vertical asymptote
signals.observation: A limit at infinity in one presentation is matched against an infinite limit at a point in another.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the description would still be right if the function were undefined at that input.
signals.name: Symbolic statement described as an equality at the point
signals.observation: The verbal description says the function equals the limit value at the input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the description names a number the function approaches.
signals.name: Unbounded growth described as reaching a value
signals.observation: The description of an infinite limit says the function becomes equal to infinity.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to mark the stated function value on the sketch and check it against the drawn point.
signals.name: Sketch satisfies the limit conditions and contradicts the value conditions
signals.observation: The curve approaches the stated heights and the plotted point at the input is drawn at the approached height rather than the stated value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what height the curve should carry just left and just right of the input.
signals.name: Sketch drawn continuous where a one sided condition demands a break
signals.observation: The two stated one sided limits differ and the sketch joins the branches.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the limit exists at the input, and whether definedness alone decides the classification.
signals.name: Break called removable because the function is undefined there
signals.observation: The response names the discontinuity removable on the grounds that the input is missing from the domain.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what value would have to be assigned at the input to close the break.
signals.name: Removable break identified with the repairing value not named
signals.observation: The classification is correct and the response does not say what value the function would need at the point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two one sided values and whether they differ.
signals.name: Jump named where the two sides agree
signals.observation: The two one sided limits are equal and the response still classifies the break as a jump.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each one sided limit is a finite number.
signals.name: Jump and infinite break not separated
signals.observation: A break where one side grows without bound is classified as a jump.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to factor both parts and say which denominator zeros survive.
signals.name: Cancelling factor reported as an asymptote
signals.observation: A zero of the original denominator that divides out is listed as a vertical asymptote.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the expression just left and just right of the input.
signals.name: Asymptote identified with no side behaviour given
signals.observation: The input is named correctly and the response does not say what the values do on each side.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each branch expression is defined everywhere on the set where it applies.
signals.name: Branch boundaries checked and excluded interior points missed
signals.observation: Every boundary is examined and an input excluded from a branch domain is left out of the list.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which branch the boundary input itself belongs to under the stated conditions.
signals.name: Boundary value taken from the branch that does not apply
signals.observation: The response substitutes the boundary input into the branch governing the other side.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to list every condition and mark which ones the response checked.
signals.name: Definedness stated as the whole of continuity
signals.observation: The response lists only that the function has a value at the point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what relation must hold between the value and the limit.
signals.name: Limit condition stated and the agreement clause omitted
signals.observation: The existence of the limit and the existence of the value are both named and their equality is not.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which condition fails and at which input.
signals.name: Definition restated in place of the failing condition
signals.observation: The response says the function is not continuous because the definition of continuity is not met.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check the named condition at the input in question.
signals.name: Correct failing condition named at the wrong input
signals.observation: The response names a genuine failure but attaches it to an input where the function is continuous.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate the function at that input.
signals.name: Excluded input left inside a reported interval
signals.observation: An input where the expression is undefined lies inside one of the intervals reported.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which expression the question is about, the original or the simplified one.
signals.name: Domain read from the simplified form only
signals.observation: The cancelled form is used to build the interval list, so an excluded input disappears.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where a member of that family fails to be defined.
signals.name: Family named as continuous everywhere rather than on its domain
signals.observation: The response says the family is continuous for every input, with no domain restriction mentioned.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which family the given expression belongs to and what its domain is.
signals.name: Family membership asserted with no check of the given expression
signals.observation: The expression is assigned to a family it does not belong to and continuity is claimed from that.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what happens at each input where the rule changes.
signals.name: Branches checked and the boundaries left unexamined
signals.observation: Each branch is declared continuous on its own and the boundary inputs are not tested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the two one sided limits at the boundary and compare them with the value.
signals.name: Boundary matched by value with the one sided limits not compared
signals.observation: The two branch expressions agree at the boundary by value and the one sided limits are never named.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the limit at the point and compare it with the value assigned.
signals.name: Value assigned that is not the limit
signals.observation: A value is supplied at the point that does not match the common one sided value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the limit exists at the input before any value is assigned.
signals.name: Repair attempted where the limit does not exist
signals.observation: A value is assigned at an input where the two one sided limits differ.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many boundaries the rule has and how many conditions that gives.
signals.name: One boundary equation written and the second omitted
signals.observation: A single equation is formed and one parameter is left undetermined or chosen arbitrarily.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what quantity must agree at each boundary for continuity to hold.
signals.name: Equations written from values with the limits not matched
signals.observation: The two branch expressions are set equal at the boundaries without reference to the one sided limits.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the limit exists at the input, as a separate question.
signals.name: Removability decided from definedness alone
signals.observation: The response says the break can be repaired because the function has no value there.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the values do near the input, and whether any single assigned value could close that.
signals.name: Infinite break called removable
signals.observation: An input where the values grow without bound is reported as repairable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the behaviour on each side separately.
signals.name: One statement written where the two sides differ in sign
signals.observation: A single infinite limit is written although one side increases and the other decreases without bound.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the symbol on the right of the equals sign names a real number.
signals.name: Infinite limit written as an existence claim
signals.observation: The response writes the limit as equal to infinity and then reports that the limit exists.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to factor both parts and identify the common factor.
signals.name: Cancellation not performed before the classification
signals.observation: The denominator zeros of the unsimplified expression are all classified as asymptotes.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many times the factor appears above and below the line.
signals.name: Cancellation performed and the multiplicity ignored
signals.observation: A factor that divides out only partly is treated as fully cancelled and the asymptote is missed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the degree of each part, then ask which case of the rule applies.
signals.name: Leading coefficients divided although the degrees differ
signals.observation: The ratio of the leading coefficients is reported without the degrees being compared.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to describe what each term does as the input grows, with nothing substituted.
signals.name: Infinity substituted into the expression
signals.observation: The infinity symbol is placed into the expression and arithmetic is performed with it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what line the curve settles towards at that end.
signals.name: Finite end behaviour value reported with no asymptote named
signals.observation: The limit at infinity is computed correctly and the horizontal asymptote is not stated when it is asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which variable is growing without bound in the statement just written.
signals.name: Vertical and horizontal asymptotes exchanged
signals.observation: A vertical asymptote is reported from an end behaviour limit, or the reverse.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the square root of the square of a negative quantity equals.
signals.name: Dominant power taken out of the radical without the sign correction
signals.observation: The work at the negative end copies the positive end and the sign of the extracted factor is not adjusted.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to write the divisor used on each part of the expression.
signals.name: Division by the dominant power applied above the line only
signals.observation: The numerator is divided by the dominant power and the expression under the radical is left undivided.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the quotient does as the input keeps growing, not what it is at one input.
signals.name: Growth compared by the values at one large input
signals.observation: The response names the larger quantity at a single sampled input rather than taking the limit of the quotient.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the computed value says about which quantity outgrows the other.
signals.name: Quotient limit computed and the comparison not stated
signals.observation: The limit of the quotient is found correctly and no conclusion about relative growth is written.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate the expression at one large negative input and compare with the claim.
signals.name: Negative end assumed to mirror the positive end
signals.observation: The value found at positive infinity is reported for negative infinity with no separate work.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which end each of the two values describes.
signals.name: Both ends computed and one written without its direction
signals.observation: Two different end values are found and the answer does not say which end each belongs to.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what must be true of the function on the interval before the theorem may be used.
signals.name: Continuity hypothesis omitted from the statement
signals.observation: The straddling condition is named and continuity on the closed interval is not.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the named theorem concludes and compare it with the conclusion reached.
